law_name: Final report of the Saeima parliamentary inquiry committee on Rail Baltica
description: Report of the inquiry committee Kulbergs chaired, presented in December 2024: 29 conclusions and 16 proposals, including a Saeima subcommittee to oversee the project. It found that the Transport Ministry had concealed the true cost increase from the Cabinet by recalculating it in 2016 prices, that the Finance Ministry's involvement had been insufficient and that the first phase was unlikely to be completed by 2030, and it named 18 people it held responsible.
significance: Supported only by opposition MPs, it set out the critique of Rail Baltica's management that Kulbergs later applied as Prime Minister.

law_name: Declaration on the intended activities of the Cabinet led by Andris Kulbergs (Deklarācija par Andra Kulberga vadītā Ministru kabineta iecerēto darbību) and coalition cooperation agreement
description: Signed on 28 May 2026 by the United List, the National Alliance, New Unity and the Union of Greens and Farmers: 52 points for the four months before the election, led by border security and anti-drone defence, 5% of GDP for defence, secure elections, action against corruption and cartels, budget stabilisation, a procurement review, Rail Baltica under the Prime Minister's direct leadership, a decision on airBaltic by August and an end to trade with Russia and Belarus. The partners undertook not to back budget-affecting proposals without consensus and not to retreat from standards on human rights, combating violence and gender equality.
significance: The basis on which the Saeima approved the government by 66 votes to 25.

law_name: Agreement between Latvia and Ukraine on comprehensive cooperation in defence ('Drone Deal')
description: Signed by Kulbergs and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Tallinn on 9 June 2026, on the sidelines of the Nordic-Baltic Eight summit. Ukraine undertakes to share expertise, particularly on unmanned systems and air defence; Latvia will support Ukraine's drone, air- and missile-defence capabilities through deliveries and by financing Ukrainian production, and plans to devote no less than 5% of its defence budget to the agreement, which can include co-production and localising defence manufacturing in Latvia.
significance: Kulbergs's first foreign visit as Prime Minister; Lithuania had signed a similar agreement with Ukraine a month earlier.

law_name: 30-day moratorium on large state ICT procurements
description: Imposed by the Prime Minister on 15 June 2026 after a meeting of the Information Society Council, to review the necessity and procedures of large information and communication technology purchases, following a procurement scandal. Kulbergs cited €452 million spent on ICT projects in 2024–2025, 38% of them handled by three companies, and criticised the practice of buying hours of work rather than finished solutions.
significance: First step of the procurement review promised in the government declaration.

law_name: Action plan of the government led by Andris Kulbergs
description: Approved by the Cabinet on 21 July 2026: 150 measures with expected results for the government's short term, derived from the declaration, plus 35 more to be implemented if additional funding is found without a negative impact on the budget. Ministries report monthly to the State Chancellery; the government said on 11 September that it had completed 16 of its 61 priority tasks.
significance: The government's own yardstick for its pre-election record.

law_name: Air Baltic Corporation Financial Stabilisation Measures Law ('Air Baltic Corporation' finanšu stabilizācijas pasākumu likums)
description: Government bill adopted in final reading on 20 August 2026 by 54 votes to 21 with one abstention (Union of Greens and Farmers against). It allows the repayment of the €30 million state loan to airBaltic to be extended to the end of 2026 and converted into shares, interest on state-held bonds to be capitalised and the bonds converted into shares, and the state to buy up to €30 million of new bonds alongside private investors on identical terms.
significance: Gave the government the mandate it used for the airline's restructuring; Kulbergs described it as a mandate rather than new money.

law_name: Restructuring of airBaltic under US Chapter 11
description: On 14 September 2026 the government announced that airBaltic, 88% state-owned, was starting a review of its debts under Chapter 11 in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York, following a plan devised by the Transport Ministry as shareholder and by the adviser Seabury Securities. The court approved debtor-in-possession financing of up to €350 million from Barclays, Hayfin, Morgan Stanley, Oaktree and Strategic Value Partners, with €175 million of the first tranche approved in full by 20 October. Kulbergs also asked for government decisions on airBaltic from the past 20 years to be declassified.
significance: The government's chosen alternative to a further state rescue loan.

law_name: Amendments to the Railway Law (Russian grain transit fees) and to the Agriculture and Rural Development Law (food import ban)
description: On 17 September 2026 the Saeima urgently amended the Railway Law to allow rail infrastructure fees for grain dispatched from Russia to be raised quickly until 31 December 2026; the government's planned 300% increase was later declared not possible by Kulbergs. On 10 September the Saeima supported in second reading a Ministry of Agriculture bill extending the national ban on imports of Russian and Belarusian agricultural products and feed, in force since March 2024, to food products, including those routed through third countries; a final reading was still required.
significance: Steps towards the declaration's pledge to stop trade with Russia and Belarus.

law_name: National sanctions on Mikhail Fridman and Alisher Usmanov
description: Cabinet order of 22 September 2026 imposing Latvian national financial and entry restrictions on the two Russian businessmen under the regulations on national sanctions against those linked to Russia's military aggression against Ukraine. Latvia is also appealing at the EU Court of Justice the lifting of EU sanctions on Fridman and Pyotr Aven.
significance: Use of Latvia's national sanctions regime alongside EU sanctions.

law_name: Cabinet decision on the scope and cost ceiling of Rail Baltica's first phase
description: Adopted at a closed emergency meeting on 1 October 2026: a ceiling of €20 million per kilometre for the main line (tracks, electrification and signalling, excluding major structures), against up to €32 million so far; a single-track embankment with the option of a second track and no more than four regional stations. The Transport Ministry must prepare a minimum project scenario by December 2026, and Latvia will assess how to review its obligations under the main-line contract signed in December 2023 with E.R.B. Rail JV.
significance: Follows the Baltic prime ministers' agreement to complete the first phase by 2034 rather than 2030.

law_name: Restrictions on new state spending commitments for the fourth quarter of 2026
description: Finance Ministry report submitted to the government on 6 October 2026: until the end of 2026 ministries and central institutions may sign new contracts for goods, consultancy, research and other external services only where needed for continuous state functions, legal compliance or procurements announced by 1 October, and must postpone non-critical spending; contracts of €50,000 or more require approval by the Prime Minister, a minister or an authorised official. The report also set out fiscal-consolidation scenarios for 2027–2030.
significance: Short-term spending brake while the 2027 budget is left to the next government.

law_name: Government decision widening border services' powers to counter threats on the eastern border
description: Decided at a closed session on 13 October 2026, after masked and armed escorts tried to push at least 20 migrants across the Belarus–Latvia border in early October. Kulbergs said, without details, that there would be 'greater scope to use kinetic measures along the country's eastern border'.
significance: Part of the border-security priority of the government declaration.
